purpose: Closed vocabulary for Qwen3-TTS synthetic voice blueprints. Every character profile selects from these values only; the renderer refuses unknown values. Values are acoustic specifications, not personality labels.

models.rule: VoiceDesign only produces reference clips. Dialogue lines are always generated by the Base model with a cached ICL prompt. Mood never reaches the Base model as text.

reference.text: Good evening. The road ahead is quiet tonight, although the weather may change before morning. Keep to the marked path, and listen for the bells. Have you brought everything you need?
rules: Every character and every mood uses this exact text. A shared script makes voices comparable and keeps ICL extraction uniform.
Do not translate, trim, or personalize the script per character.
Reject a recording shorter than 8 s or longer than 18 s; regenerate with the same seed offset instead of editing the audio.
Store the exact transcript with every generated clip; ICL requires ref_text to match the audio word for word.
The open-weight model has a reported ICL startup artifact where the first words of the reference leak into the output. Check the first 2 s of a new profile before approving it.

presentation.question: How is the voice heard, not what the character's body or gender identity is?

masculine.notes: Perceived male vocal production. Default for male characters.

feminine.notes: Perceived female vocal production. Default for female characters.

androgynous.notes: Deliberately ambiguous. Requires explicit evidence; do not infer from an unknown sex field.

neutral.notes: Minimal gender cue. Use for narrators, generic voices, and characters whose presentation is unstated.

nonhuman.notes: Beast, lifeless, or ethereal timbre. Experimental: Qwen3-TTS is a speech model and may render this as an odd human voice. Always audition.

synthetic.notes: Mammets, nodes, Allagan constructs. Experimental, audition required.

perceived_age.question: How old does the voice sound, not how old the character is in lore years?
notes: Use perceived vocal age. A 100-year-old Elezen may sound like a young adult; a 30-year-old Lalafell still sounds adult, never childlike.
Null is allowed and preferred over a guess. The renderer simply omits the age clause.
Never combine an age with a presentation that contradicts it (child + mature); one value only by construction.
Register describes where the voice sits, not how expressive it is.
Body size and race are not sufficient evidence for a register; they are at most creative_selection.
Extreme ends (very_low, very_high) require explicit or supported_inference evidence.
Optional. Omit when unsure; the model defaults to a natural range.

timbre_primary.question: What is the dominant texture of the voice?
notes: This is the single most differentiating field after pitch. Spend the creative effort here.
Values that share a family are acoustically redundant; the validator rejects combining two of them (husky + gravelly is one instruction, not two).
At most one secondary texture, from a different family than the primary.
Two overlapping roughness words muddle the instruction; three guarantee mush.
Preferred secondary use is a light modifier: slightly breathy, slightly nasal, a hint of reediness.
Optional. Omit rather than guess; a wrong resonance clause is a bigger error than a missing one.
How consonants and vowels are formed. Default for ordinary NPCs is relaxed or crisp.
slurred, drawling, staccato, and sharp are acting choices and require explicit or supported_inference evidence.
Pace is a rhythm property of the voice, not an emotion. An angry character is not automatically fast.
measured and moderate cover most NPCs; very_slow and very_fast need evidence.
Default natural. Prefer natural or restrained; dramatic and melodic make a character's every line theatrical.
Personality traits such as stoic or arrogant may justify restrained, but only as supported_inference.
Profile and strength are set together or both omitted; the validator rejects half an accent.
Qwen3-TTS has no accent mode. Accent clauses are soft hints; verify by listening before approving a profile.
Never derive an accent from a nation or race alone. Use the project default when the wiki says nothing.
The project default is evidence level 'default', never 'explicit'.
Embellishments, never mandatory. Omit most of the time.
A trait whose family matches an already selected timbre, resonance, or articulation is redundant and is rejected.

moods.status: generated per character and auditioned; not per-line
moods.purpose: The mood layer is a separate reference recording per state. It exists so the same identity can be performed in different emotional registers without redrawing the character.
implementation_rules: A mood is baked into its own VoiceDesign reference clip and its own cached ICL prompt. It is never passed to the Base model as text.
The identity prompt is identical across a character's archons; only the trailing mood block differs.
Every archon speaks the same reference script as the neutral clip.
NEVER select an archon per dialogue line. Listening on 2026-11-01 found the shift between archons far too large: the same character would change voice mid-conversation.
Archon choice is a casting decision made once per character, recorded in pack_archon, and defaulting to neutral.
Neutral is the basis. It is deliberately the least expressive of the archons and is what every character packs with until a source justifies otherwise.
Add an archon only when the source material describes how the character sounds by default, not when a scene happens to be emotional.
Every character needs a neutral archon. Mood archons are optional and are auditioned against each other before one is chosen for packing.
rules: The neutral variant is the identity prompt alone. It exists as a preset only so a profile can override it; with no overrides the renderer emits no mood block and the identity text is used verbatim.
Presets are the only moods. Do not invent free-form mood names.
Overrides may change at most two fields from the preset; a third override means the preset is wrong and should be corrected here first.
Reserve extreme intensity for a deliberate decision; ordinary dialogue lives at subtle to moderate.
shouting and whispering are production styles, not emotions; do not use them as the default mood of a character.
moods.definition: One mood reference is an ARCHON: a designed reference clip plus its cached ICL prompt. A character owns a small set of archons (neutral plus whichever moods the source justifies). A pack uses exactly one archon for all of that character's lines, and that archon's clip is pinned by hash.

archon_pinning.unit: the reference clip, not a per-line seed
archon_pinning.rule: One approved reference WAV per archon is stored and hashed. Every dialogue line for that character is cloned from that clip through create_voice_clone_prompt, so identity is fixed without seeding individual lines.
archon_pinning.why_not_a_line_seed: Measured 2026-11-01: two lines from the same take score 0.991-0.994 cosine, two lines from different takes 0.984-0.994, and per-line pitch scatter inside one take exceeds the mean gap between takes. A line seed does not carry identity.
archon_pinning.why_not_only_a_design_seed: The same seed produces a different clip when dtype, attention backend, torch build, or the reference script change. The hash is the durable guarantee; the design seed is kept for reproducibility.

render.identity_template: {article} {age}{presentation} voice{pitch}{pitch_range}. It has a {timbre}{timbre_secondary}{resonance}. Speech is {articulation} with {intonation} intonation, at a {pace} pace{accent}.{traits} Neutral conversational delivery for game dialogue.
render.mood_template: For this take, speak with {phrase}, at {intensity} emotional intensity. Use {energy} vocal energy, {projection} projection, and a {pace} speaking pace. The delivery should carry {pitch_movement} intonation, {articulation} articulation, and {rhythm} rhythm.
render.mood_composition: mood_instruct = identity_prompt + ' ' + mood_template(rendered). The identity text is byte-identical across every mood of a character; only the trailing mood block changes.
render.article_rule: Use 'An' when the rendered phrase starts with a vowel sound (adult, ageless, ancient, elderly, androgynous), otherwise 'A'.
render.banned_identity_words_reason: Identity is the constant; emotion belongs to the mood layer. An emotion word in the identity prompt makes every line of the character permanently emotional.
render.word_target_note: 48 is the hard ceiling: it still fits accent plus secondary timbre plus two traits. Anything longer dilutes the description, and Qwen's own voice-design examples are shorter.

values.explicit: The wiki states it directly (age, gender, race, or a described voice).
values.supported_inference: Several wiki statements point the same way (consistently described as soft-spoken or formal).
values.creative_selection: Chosen to differentiate the character within the vocabulary; no source claim.
values.default: Project fallback applied because no information exists.
values.unknown: No reliable information; field left null.

rules: Every non-null identity field carries an evidence entry with a level.
explicit and supported_inference require a source URL and a short quote.
creative_selection and default require neither, but must be self-evidently plausible.
unknown is only valid on nullable fields.

allowed: Race and sex feed presentation and perceived_age.
Stated age or an age range feeds perceived_age.
Explicit voice description in prose feeds pitch, timbre, pace, or articulation.
Occupation and upbringing may feed articulation (refined, clipped, drawling) as supported_inference.
Social role may feed intonation (ceremonial, restrained) as supported_inference.
forbidden: Race, height, build, or body mass as evidence for pitch or timbre.
Occupation as evidence for timbre or pitch (every blacksmith does not sound gravelly).
Personality as evidence for pitch, timbre, or age (every cheerful character does not get a high pitch).
Mood words as identity fields at all.
Adding emotion to the identity prompt because the character is usually emotional.
Inventing an age or accent for a character with no sourced information.
inference_policy.required_for_allowed_inferences: Body-based or role-based choices are creative_selection, never explicit. A reviewer must be able to see that the value was a design choice.

profile_rules: One canonical profile per NPC id. Labels that resolve to the same NPC share the profile.
Unnamed or generic labels get a bank archetype profile, not a new invented voice.
A character profile never stores audio, seeds, or paths; reference recordings and cached prompts live in the generated voice directory.
profiles are versioned; bump profile_version whenever a selected value changes, so already-generated lines can be traced to the voice that produced them.

checks: reference_duration_ok: the neutral clip is 10-15 s.
reference_transcript_verified: the stored transcript matches the audio word for word.
no_reference_leak: the first 2 s of a held-out clone do not repeat the reference tail.
identity_approved: a human listened and accepted the voice as the character.
no_drift: two independent clone lines are recognisably the same speaker.
